jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleAssistant Professor Potato and Sugarbeet Pathology Next JobApply for JobJob ID2959938 Business UnitNorth Dakota State University LocationFargo Posted09/23/2026 Full/Part TimePart-Time DepartmentAES Plant Path, Micro &Biotech Close DateOpen Until Filled Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job Position Information The Department of Plant Pathology, Microbiology, and Biotechnology (PPMB) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position. The successful applicant will: 1) join over two-dozen faculty in a recently merged department with established histories of high-quality and high-impact research and Extension with excellent undergraduate and graduate programs, 2) join a team of collaborative pathologists and other scientists working to help the industry produce and protect potatoes and sugarbeets, and 3) collaborate with a broader team of public- and private-sector professionals and stakeholders. The successful candidate will be eligible for nomination to the John T. Nordgaard Endowed Faculty Professorship, which provides support for salary, potato pathology research, graduate student stipends, and teaching. Responsibilities: The appointment is 80% research (North Dakota Agriculture Experiment Station), 10% teaching (College of Agriculture, Food Systems, and Natural Resources) and 10% service. The successful candidate will develop and lead a regionally-, nationally- and internationally-recognized research program that addresses established and emerging diseases that threaten the production, storage and profitability of potatoes and sugarbeets. The position is open to all areas of plant disease research, with opportunities to collaborate and conduct complementary research with faculty, USDA researchers and other university researchers working on potato and sugarbeet pathology. The successful applicant will advise graduate students, teach in areas that utilize their expertise and fit the needs of the department, engage in outreach to stakeholders, and contribute service to PPMB, NDSU and professional societies. Qualifications: Minimum qualifications are: an earned Ph.D. in plant pathology or a closely related field with extensive background in plant pathology at the time of hire; demonstrated ability to conduct and publish research in high-quality and relevant journals; demonstrated experience in applied research; strong communication skills (interpersonal, written, verbal, etc.); capacity to work effectively, cooperatively, and collegially with a diverse population of stakeholders, colleagues, students, and scientists from other disciplines. Preferred qualifications are: professional experience beyond a Ph.D. (such as post-doc or industry); demonstrated experience obtaining extramural funding and publishing refereed journal articles from such funding; demonstrated experience using modern and traditional techniques for potato/sugarbeet disease research; evidence of effective teaching and/or pedagogical training; experience mentoring and/or managing students and/or staff. Application: Review of applications will begin October 20, 2026. jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleAssistant Professor/Extension Sugarbeet Agronomist Next JobApply for JobJob ID2959848 Business UnitNorth Dakota State University LocationFargo Posted09/02/2026 Full/Part TimeFull-Time DepartmentExt Plant Science Close DateOpen Until Filled Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job Position Information Description & Details:This is a 12-month, tenure-track position (70% Extension, 20% research, and 10% service) in the Department of Plant Sciences at North Dakota State University. The position is jointly funded by North Dakota State University (NDSU) and the University of Minnesota (U of M). The incumbent will be based at NDSU and expected to work in both North Dakota and Minnesota. The successful candidate will lead the development and implementation of Extension and applied research programs focused on weed management and cropping systems for sugarbeet production. Responsibilities include developing educational materials and programs for producers, industry professionals, and Extension personnel; conducting applied research; publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and Extension publications; delivering science-based recommendations to support successful sugarbeet production; and pursuing extramural funding. The incumbent will build collaborative partnerships (including equipment and resources) with NDSU faculty and staff, specifically in the NDSU Departments of Plant Sciences and Plant Pathology, Microbiology, and Biotechnology; with the University of Minnesota; the Sugarbeet Research and Education Board; USDA sugarbeet researchers; allied industry partners in the sugarbeet industry; and sugarbeet cooperatives. Extension programming will use a variety of delivery methods, including print and digital publications, web resources, presentations, field days, workshops, radio, television, and virtual platforms. Additional responsibilities include coordinating Extension and research activities across department and college faculty and Extension agents across a range of agronomic disciplines, and advising graduate students.Hiring Range: $85,000 +Pay is based on several factors, including budget, labor market, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and/or certification and other business considerations. Minimum Qualifications:An earned PhD in weed science, crop science, agronomy, or a related field by the hire date.Demonstrated experience in applied crop production and/or in weed management.Demonstrated ability to work effectively with university faculty, Extension personnel, producer organizations, and the public.Demonstrated ability to conduct applied research, interpret and communicate findings, and develop science-based recommendations for producers.Proven ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders, colleagues, and multidisciplinary research teams. Proficiency with computer applications and relevant technologies.Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.Possession of a valid US driver's license or the ability to obtain one by the date of hire.Possession of, or ability to obtain by the hire date, a valid pesticide applicator’s license in North Dakota and Minnesota. Preferred Qualifications:Farm background or practical agricultural production experience.Experience with sugarbeet production systems.Experience in Extension, teaching, stakeholder engagement, or agricultural outreach.Research, industry, or applied agricultural experience in crop production and weed management.Demonstrated success in developing competitive grant proposals, securing extramural funding, and publishing research findings.Knowledge of agricultural regulations and experience navigating regulatory frameworks.Experience with precision agriculture, crop data management, or related digital agriculture technologies.Application Deadline:October 1, 2026, or until filled. jobs.title: Chair, Department of Art and Design, Associate or Full Professor, Tenured
jobs.description: Chair, Department of Art and Design, Associate or Full Professor, Tenured 499293 Grand Forks, North Dakota, United States Full-time Faculty View favorites Salary/Position Classification Associate Professor $75,000+, Full Professor $85,000+, commensurate with experience 9-month contract, Exempt 40 hours per week 100% Remote Work Availability: No Hybrid Work Availability (requires some time on campus): No Purpose of Position The Department of Art & Design at the University of North Dakota is seeking an Associate or Full Professor in studio art or art history. Candidates must hold an MFA in a studio art discipline or a Ph.D. in art history and demonstrate a record of professional accomplishments commensurate with appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure. Appointment is subject to review and approval by the Department, College, University, and North Dakota State Board of Higher Education. This is a nine-month, tenured faculty appointment with an additional part-time summer contract while serving as Department Chair, contingent upon the availability of funding. The Department of Art & Design is housed in the College of Arts & Sciences and currently offers an MFA in Visual Arts, BFAs in Visual Arts and Graphic Design, a BA in Visual Arts, and minors in Art History, Graphic Design, and Visual Arts. The department is the recipient of a generous annually recurring endowment from the Myers Foundations that supports a robust visiting artists program, curation of art exhibitions, and resources to enhance student teaching and learning among other activities. Established in 1883, the University of North Dakota is the oldest research university in North Dakota. Founded with a strong liberal arts foundation, it is the state’s flagship university and is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as having very high research activity. UND offers degrees in more than 225 fields of study and enrolls nearly 16,000 students. It is the home of the state’s only School of Law and School of Medicine. The School of Medicine and Health Sciences has major initiatives in rural and public health, and Aerospace is home to one of the first and largest unmanned aerial vehicle programs in the world. UND is located in Grand Forks, North Dakota, a vibrant college town of over 57,000 people located on the border of North Dakota and Minnesota. Short commutes, a great public-school system, high-quality medical facilities, low crime, ample parks and theaters, and a cost of living below that found in large American cities are some of Grand Forks’ advantages. Ranked as one of the top 5 Best Small College Towns, and America’s Best Hockey Town, Grand Forks offers stellar quality of life without the metropolitan hassles. UND and the College of Arts & Sciences value diverse perspectives and seek applicants to help students succeed. The University of North Dakota is supportive of dual-career assistance both within the University and the local community. jobs.description: Work Well Instructor 499361 Grand Forks, North Dakota, United States Federal Work Study Student Institutional Student Closing on: Oct 16 2026 View favorites Salary/Position Classification $14.00 hourly, Non-Exempt (Eligible for overtime) 4-6 hours per week (the hours for this position will be morning to afternoon with some evening hours required) 100% Remote Work Availability: No Hybrid Work Availability (requires some time on campus): No Purpose of Position Work Well Instructors lead faculty and staff in a group environment, through a pre-arranged format of exercises designed to de-stress and enhance body functioning through stretching and mobility, while ensuring the safety of the members is not compromised. Instructors will also serve as a resource to educate members on various aspects of fitness. This is a part-time, non-benefited position. Only UND students are eligible to be hired in this position. Duties & Responsibilities Effectively lead participants through established group exercise formats Performs a well-organized class, safety, ROM, and educates participants in proper form Adjust class to accommodate a variety of fitness levels Engages and connects with participants, approachable, and caters to needs of members Assist in the development of new classes and methods of instructing. Disseminate information on all Work Well services and programs. Utilize appropriate technology to track participation. Complete all cleaning and sanitation tasks as assigned to maintain a safe & healthy environment. Must wear appropriate PPE as directed for specific tasks/duties. Attend all meetings/trainings as required. Required Competencies As a result of working in this position, the staff member will gain the following skills: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving Interpersonal Development Intrapersonal Development Professionalism Minimum Requirements General working knowledge of all group exercise movements and ability to explain proper technique to participants. Has effective coaching skills and knowledge in exercise physiology Ability to effectively communicate with participants and provide motivation for continued participation in physical activity and healthy living. Certification in CPR/First Aid/AED, or ability to obtain within 2 weeks of hire. (Training provided by the Wellness Center at no cost for employees) Successful completion of a Criminal History Background Check In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the US and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. This position does not support visa sponsorship for continued employment. Preferred Qualifications Hold or be pursuing a major or minor in exercise science, recreation, nutrition or health-related field OR have experience in Group Exercise and/or at least one certification but pursuing a different primary career. Ability to demonstrate a competent level of instructing skills or have prior instructing experience.
